literature.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒持续威胁全球公共卫生。
literature.lead_zh: 尼帕病毒自1998年在马来西亚首次出现后,多次暴发并具有高致死率,其传播模式已从猪源性转向蝙蝠源性。
key_findings_zh: 尼帕病毒传播模式从猪源性转向蝙蝠源性 [10.1002/rmv.70221]。
尼帕病毒感染可导致急性脑炎和广泛内皮损伤 [10.1002/rmv.70221]。
印度近期暴发凸显病毒在人口密集区的防控挑战 [10.1002/rmv.70221]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 尼帕病毒的传播风险持续上升,尤其在人口密集地区。
literature.caveats_zh: 目前尚无针对人类的获批疫苗,治疗手段有限。
literature.headline_en: Nipah Virus Continues to Pose a Global Public Health Threat.
literature.lead_en: Since its emergence in Malaysia in 1998, Nipah virus has repeatedly caused outbreaks and remains a significant threat to global public health.
key_findings_en: Nipah virus transmission has shifted from pigs to Pteropus fruit bats, contaminated food, and close human contact [10.1002/rmv.70221]
Nipah virus infection is associated with severe respiratory involvement, immune dysregulation, and acute encephalitis [10.1002/rmv.70221]
Recent outbreaks in India highlight the challenges of outbreak containment in densely populated areas [10.1002/rmv.70221]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The risk of Nipah virus outbreaks is increasing, particularly in densely populated regions.
literature.caveats_en: There is currently no licensed vaccine for human use, and therapeutic options remain limited.
literature.brief_en: Nipah virus remains a significant global health threat with high mortality rates and evolving transmission patterns, particularly from fruit bats. Recent outbreaks in India emphasize the need for improved diagnostics and containment strategies.

A probe was announced into whether expired doses of Remdesivir were given to Nipah patients. The Health Minister admitted that expired doses may have been administered between 2023 and 2025, sparking political controversy. [news-c78ac4d7c1e5e955]

papers.title: Nipah Virus (NiV) in Focus: Molecular Insights Into Pathogenesis, Transmission Dynamics, and Evolving Epidemiology From Malaysia to Recent Indian Outbreaks.
papers.abstract: Since the emergence of the Nipah virus (NiV) in Malaysia in 1998, it has returned multiple times and continues to pose a significant threat to global public health. It is characterised by high mortality and fatality rates and increasing evidence of human-to-human transmission. The epidemiological pattern of NiV has shifted considerably over the past 2 decades, from transmission primarily associated with infected pigs to repeated spillover events linked to Pteropus fruit bats, contaminated food sources, and close human contact. NiV infection is marked by severe respiratory involvement, immune dysregulation, acute encephalitis and widespread endothelial damage contributing to rapid clinical deterioration and poor outcomes. The World Health Organisation classified the Nipah virus as a priority pathogen with high mortality and pandemic potential, with recognised outbreaks showing case fatalities ranging from 40% to 100%. The virus has been detected in the Indian subcontinent and is carried by fruit bats. Recent outbreaks reported in India through 2026 have further highlighted the ongoing threat posed by the virus and the challenges of outbreak containment in densely populated regions. Current advances in serological and Molecular diagnostics have improved early detection; however, therapeutic options remain limited, and no licenced vaccine is currently available for human use. Ongoing therapeutics research involving monoclonal antibodies, recombinant vaccines, and antiviral agent platforms continues to expand the prospects for future prevention and disease control. Outbreaks must be prevented by prompt diagnosis and the application of infection control measures. However, the lack of knowledge regarding the pathophysiology, clinical features, and current treatment of Nipah virus disease makes it difficult to design such trials. The current advances summarised herein strengthen the scientific foundation for improved diagnostic platforms, antiviral interventions, vaccine development, and integrated One Health surveillance approaches targeting Nipah Virus.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides a detailed analysis of Nipah virus (NiV) and its associated disease, focusing on molecular insights into pathogenesis, transmission dynamics, and evolving epidemiology. The virus has re-emerged multiple times since its initial outbreak in Malaysia in 1998, with increasing evidence of human-to-human transmission. The epidemiological pattern has shifted from pig-associated transmission to spillover events linked to Pteropus fruit bats, contaminated food, and close human contact. NiV infection is characterised by severe respiratory involvement, immune dysregulation, acute encephalitis, and widespread endothelial damage, leading to rapid clinical deterioration and high mortality rates. The World Health Organisation has classified NiV as a priority pathogen with pandemic potential. Despite recent advances in diagnostics, therapeutic options remain limited, and no licensed vaccine is available. The review highlights the need for improved outbreak containment strategies, including prompt diagnosis and infection control measures, as well as ongoing research into monoclonal antibodies, recombinant vaccines, and antiviral agents.

It is characterised by high mortality and fatality rates and increasing evidence of human-to-human transmission. The epidemiological pattern of NiV has shifted considerably over the past 2 decades, from transmission primarily associated with infected pigs to repeated spillover events linked to Pteropus fruit bats, contaminated food sources, and close human contact. NiV infection is marked by severe respiratory involvement, immune dysregulation, acute encephalitis and widespread endothelial damage contributing to rapid clinical deterioration and poor outcomes. The World Health Organisation classified the Nipah virus as a priority pathogen with high mortality and pandemic potential, with recognised outbreaks showing case fatalities ranging from 40% to 100%. The virus has been detected in the Indian subcontinent and is carried by fruit bats. Recent outbreaks reported in India through 2026 have further highlighted the ongoing threat posed by the virus and the challenges of outbreak containment in densely populated regions. Current advances in serological and Molecular diagnostics have improved early detection; however, therapeutic options remain limited, and no licenced vaccine is currently available for human use. Ongoing therapeutics research involving monoclonal antibodies, recombinant vaccines, and antiviral agent platforms continues to expand the prospects for future prevention and disease control. Outbreaks must be prevented by prompt diagnosis and the application of infection control measures. However, the lack of knowledge regarding the pathophysiology, clinical features, and current treatment of Nipah virus disease makes it difficult to design such trials. The current advances summarised herein strengthen the scientific foundation for improved diagnostic platforms, antiviral interventions, vaccine development, and integrated One Health surveillance approaches targeting Nipah Virus.

papers.title: Nanobodies targeting a conserved henipavirus G glycoprotein receptor-binding region potently protect against Nipah virus infection.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV) are highly lethal zoonotic henipaviruses with pandemic potential, yet no approved antiviral therapeutics are currently available. Here, we identified four nanobodies targeting the viral attachment glycoprotein (G) with strong neutralizing activity. All candidates potently neutralized NiV-Malaysia (NiV M ) and NiV-Bangladesh (NiV B ) in authentic virus assays, with IC 50 values in the low ng/mL range (2.50-18.3 ng/mL). 2E2 shows the most potent activity, with an IC 50 of 2.50 ng/mL. These candidates cross-neutralized HeV in pseudovirus assays at levels comparable to those against NiV, yet authentic HeV neutralization was reduced with the most potent clone reaching an IC50 of 160 ng/mL and the remaining clones showing variable potency. In Syrian hamsters challenged with 1000 LD 50 NiV M , prophylactic administration of 1C3, 2E2, or 5A3 provides complete protection. Notably, 2E2 confers superior therapeutic protection (66.7% survival) when administered 24 h post-infection. Additionally, 2E2 provides 50% prophylactic protection against lethal HeV. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis indicated that the nanobodies recognize a conserved region within the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of G, with distinct sensitivities to individual residue substitutions. Notably, 2E2 exhibited minimal sensitivity to the tested NiV G mutations and retained neutralizing activity against the m102.4 escape-associated substitutions NiV G-V507I and HeV G-D582N. These findings identify 2E2 as a candidate RBD-targeting nanobody with potent prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy against NiV and cross-neutralizing activity against HeV, warranting further evaluation as a countermeasure for NiV outbreaks.

papers.title_zh: 靶向保守的 亨尼帕病毒 G 糖蛋白受体结合区的纳米抗体可有效防止 亨尼帕病毒 感染。
papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) and Hendra virus (HeV) are highly lethal zoonotic henipaviruses with pandemic potential, yet no approved antiviral therapeutics are currently available. Here, we identified four nanobodies targeting the viral attachment glycoprotein (G) with strong neutralizing activity. All candidates potently neutralized NiV-Malaysia (NiV M ) and NiV-Bangladesh (NiV B ) in authentic virus assays, with IC 50 values in the low ng/mL range (2.50-18.3 ng/mL). 2E2 shows the most potent activity, with an IC 50 of 2.50 ng/mL. These candidates cross-neutralized HeV in pseudovirus assays at levels comparable to those against NiV, yet authentic HeV neutralization was reduced with the most potent clone reaching an IC50 of 160 ng/mL and the remaining clones showing variable potency. In Syrian hamsters challenged with 1000 LD 50 NiV M , prophylactic administration of 1C3, 2E2, or 5A3 provides complete protection. Notably, 2E2 confers superior therapeutic protection (66.7% survival) when administered 24 h post-infection. Additionally, 2E2 provides 50% prophylactic protection against lethal HeV. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis indicated that the nanobodies recognize a conserved region within the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of G, with distinct sensitivities to individual residue substitutions. Notably, 2E2 exhibited minimal sensitivity to the tested NiV G mutations and retained neutralizing activity against the m102.4 escape-associated substitutions NiV G-V507I and HeV G-D582N. These findings identify 2E2 as a candidate RBD-targeting nanobody with potent prophylactic and therapeutic efficacy against NiV and cross-neutralizing activity against HeV, warranting further evaluation as a countermeasure for NiV outbreaks.

papers.title: A Synthetic Consensus Chiroptera IFN-β Induces IFN-I Signaling Across Diverse Bat Taxa
papers.abstract: Bat-associated viruses consistently spill over from bats into humans and other animals. Many bat-associated viruses, including Marburg virus and Nipah virus, cause severe disease in humans but their presentation is subclinical in bats. Advancements in tools and resources to study bat innate antiviral immune responses, including the type I IFN (IFN-I) pathway, are needed to evaluate the mechanisms that underlie differential infection outcomes between reservoir bats and spillover hosts. Commercially available IFN-Is are not bat-specific, and conspecific IFN-Is are impractical to produce for the over 1,500 described bat species. Here, we design and validate a bat order-level consensus IFN (Chiroptera IFN-β) that is functional in bat cells from six diverse bat families, including representatives from both suborders. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, we demonstrate that Chiroptera IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to conspecific IFN-β. This valuable resource can accelerate the capacity of the field to study bat innate antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans.

papers.source_body_en: Bat-associated viruses consistently spill over from bats into humans and other animals. Many bat-associated viruses, including Marburg virus and Nipah virus, cause severe disease in humans but their presentation is subclinical in bats. Advancements in tools and resources to study bat innate antiviral immune responses, including the type I IFN (IFN-I) pathway, are needed to evaluate the mechanisms that underlie differential infection outcomes between reservoir bats and spillover hosts. Commercially available IFN-Is are not bat-specific, and conspecific IFN-Is are impractical to produce for the over 1,500 described bat species. Here, we design and validate a bat order-level consensus IFN (Chiroptera IFN-β) that is functional in bat cells from six diverse bat families, including representatives from both suborders. Using Jamaican fruit bat cells, we demonstrate that Chiroptera IFN-β induces an IFN-stimulated gene repertoire comparable to conspecific IFN-β. This valuable resource can accelerate the capacity of the field to study bat innate antiviral responses and illuminate differences between bats and humans.

papers.title: DeepMolVir: Learning Virtual Virus Representations for Sequence-Aware Virus–Inhibitor Activity Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus–inhibitor interactions. However, most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information. Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound–virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning. Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound–virus interactions. In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Notably, virtual virus representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing. Collectively, our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery. Code and data are available at GitHub: https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir.
papers.journal: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

The authors highlight the limitations of existing computational models that treat viruses as categorical identifiers rather than capturing sequence-level biological information.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved assembling a dataset of 50,711 compound–virus activity pairs across 178 viral species and exploring protein language models for viral representation learning. The focus was on Nipah virus and its associated disease, with the goal of developing a sequence-aware approach for antiviral activity prediction.
analysis_en.methods: The authors used embeddings generated by ESMC-600M to create virtual virus representations, encoding viruses as sequence-derived biological entities rather than taxonomic labels. These representations were integrated with molecular features to model compound–virus interactions through a deep learning framework.
analysis_en.main_results: In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir achieved an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Virtual virus representations outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, and ablation studies confirmed that viral sequence information was a key contributor to model performance.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret their findings as establishing protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction. analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more accurate computational tools for antiviral discovery, particularly for Nipah virus and related diseases. papers.title_zh: DeepMolVir:学习虚拟病毒表示以进行序列感知病毒抑制剂活性预测
papers.source_body_en: Abstract The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus–inhibitor interactions. However, most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information. Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound–virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning. Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound–virus interactions. In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Notably, virtual virus representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing. Collectively, our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery. Code and data are available at GitHub: https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 新出现的耐药病毒的威胁日益严重,需要有效的方法来预测病毒与抑制剂的相互作用。然而,大多数现有的计算模型将病毒视为分类标识符,无法捕获序列级的生物信息。在这里,我们收集了涵盖 178 个病毒物种的 50,711 个复合病毒活性对的数据集,并探索了蛋白质语言模型作为病毒表征学习的策略。使用 ESMC-600M 生成的嵌入,我们引入了一种虚拟病毒表示,其中病毒被编码为序列衍生的生物实体,而不是分类标签。这些病毒表征与分子特征相结合,以模拟化合物与病毒的相互作用。在广泛的 5 倍交叉验证中,DeepMolVir 表现出了强大的预测性能,实现了 0.8653 的 AUC 和 0.9480 的 RMSE。值得注意的是,虚拟病毒表示始终优于传统的基于分类学的编码,而消融研究强调病毒序列信息是模型性能的关键贡献者。尼帕病毒 和汉坦病毒的案例研究进一步证明了 DeepMolVir 识别候选 抗病毒药物 支架和支持跨家族药物再利用的能力。总的来说,我们的研究结果确立了基于蛋白质语言模型的病毒表示学习作为序列感知 抗病毒药物 活动预测的有效策略,并为计算 抗病毒药物 发现提供了基础。代码和数据可在 GitHub 上获取:https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir。

Recognising the growing threat posed by the virus and its emergence in countries of the WHO South-East Asia Region, WHO South-East Asia Regional Office (SEARO) designated Nipah virus as a regional priority pathogen in 2018. To strengthen regional preparedness and response, WHO subsequently developed the South-East Asia Regional Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Nipah Virus Infection 2023–2030, which provides a comprehensive framework for prevention, preparedness, detection, response, and resilience against Nipah virus infection across the Region. Addressing a critical evidence gap Although Nipah virus infection continues to be associated with high case fatality ratios, the ability to accurately predict which patients are at greatest risk of severe disease and poor outcomes remains limited. Standardised and validated disease severity scores could help address this challenge. Recognising the importance of developing a standardised Nipah disease severity score (DSS), a critical tool for outbreak response, clinical research, and vaccine evaluation, WHO SEARO collaborated with the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) and PATH to convene a stakeholder consultation under the CEPI’s Nipah Vaccine Outbreak Trial Planning and Preparedness (NiVOTriPP) Project. WHO, CEPI and PATH convened a stakeholder consultation in Kathmandu, Nepal, from 11 to 13 August to advance the development of a Nipah disease severity score. (Photo credit: CEPI) The NiVOTriPP project was initiated to develop a scenario-specific, flexible, and adaptive clinical trial protocol for evaluation of Nipah vaccine efficacy (VE) in case of a potentially large outbreak (i.e., Nipah-X). While the current epidemiology of Nipah virus disease makes it practically infeasible to evaluate VE, any change in epidemiology leading to larger outbreaks may allow conduct of such trials. NiVOTriPP is set up to prepare for such a potential scenario. The DSS is being developed in parallel with the protocol under NiVOTriPP, and its primary purpose is to support vaccine evaluation in clinical trials by enabling the standardised and consistent measurement of disease severity during Nipah virus outbreaks. The consultation also responded to calls for strengthening public-private partnerships in the development of medical countermeasures and for promoting research collaboration as outlined in the implementation framework of the WHO South-East Asia Regional Strategy for the Prevention and Control of Nipah Virus Infection 2023–2030. Bringing together multidisciplinary expertise The consultation brought together international and regional experts in Nipah virus surveillance, outbreak response, vaccine trial design in outbreak settings, clinical management, biostatistics and disease severity score development. The primary objective of the consultation was to obtain expert input on the factors to be included in the scoring system and the methodological approaches for possible derivation, refinement, and validation. During the three-day meeting, participants reviewed the available evidence and identified the most relevant clinical signs, symptoms, and other factors for inclusion in the DSS. Experts also reviewed methodological approaches for score development, refinement, and validation. The consultation brought together multidisciplinary experts from across the WHO South-East Asia Region and beyond. (Photo credit: CEPI) Next steps An initial draft DSS was developed based on the discussions and consensus reached during the consultation. Further review and refinement will be undertaken through a series of technical working group activities during the next phase of the project. WHO SEARO, CEPI, and PATH will continue to partner on refining and validating the draft DSS. In addition to its primary intended use as a standardised, evidence-based tool for estimating vaccine efficacy in forthcoming studies, the DSS has the potential to support therapeutic research and improve clinical management of Nipah virus disease across the region. news.title_zh: WHO、CEPI 和 PATH 合作开发标准化尼帕病严重程度评分,以加强 暴发 的准备工作和 疫苗 研究 - 世界卫生组织 (WHO)
news.source_body_en: The World Health Organization (WHO), the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), and PATH have collaborated to develop a standardized Nipah disease severity score (DSS) to enhance outbreak preparedness and vaccine research. This initiative was announced on 30 October 2026, with a stakeholder consultation held in Kathmandu, Nepal, from 11 to 13 August 2026. The DSS aims to address the high case fatality ratios of Nipah virus infection and improve the prediction of severe disease outcomes. The collaboration focuses on the WHO South-East Asia Region, which includes countries such as Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand, and Timor-Leste. The development of the DSS is part of the NiVOTriPP project, which seeks to create a flexible and adaptive clinical trial protocol for evaluating Nipah vaccine efficacy in the event of large outbreaks. The status of the initiative is under investigation as the scoring system is being refined and validated. This effort is critical for strengthening public-private partnerships and promoting research collaboration in the region.
news.content_zh: 世界卫生组织 (WHO)、流行病防范创新联盟 (CEPI) 和 PATH 合作开发了标准化的尼帕疾病严重程度评分 (DSS),以加强 暴发 的防范和 疫苗 研究。该举措于 2026 年 10 月 30 日宣布,并于 2026 年 8 月 11 日至 13 日在尼泊尔加德满都举行了利益相关者磋商。DSS 旨在解决 尼帕病毒 感染的高病死率问题,并改进对严重疾病结果的预测。此次合作的重点是世卫组织东南亚区域,其中包括孟加拉国、不丹、印度、马尔代夫、缅甸、尼泊尔、斯里兰卡、泰国和东帝汶等国家。DSS 的开发是 NiVOTriPP 项目的一部分,该项目旨在创建一个灵活且适应性强的临床试验方案,用于评估 Nipah 疫苗 在大 暴发 事件中的疗效。随着评分系统的完善和验证,该计划的状态正在接受调查。这项努力对于加强该地区的公私伙伴关系和促进研究合作至关重要。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, November 3, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Technology Memory Effects and Optimal Control Reshape Nipah Virus Spillover in Fractional Multi-Host Model by October 29, 2026 in Technology Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Memory Effects and Optimal Control Reshape Nipah Virus Spillover in Fractional Multi-Host Model Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Mathematicians have built a fractional-order epidemic model that tracks Nipah virus transmission simultaneously across human, pig, and bird populations, and paired it with an optimal control framework to identify the most effective intervention strategies. The study, published as open access research in Discover Analytics on 13 July 2026 by Sunday Oluwafemi Gbodogbe and Adedapo Chris Loyinmi, formulates the model using the Caputo fractional derivative, an operator that incorporates memory effects arising from past infection states, which classical integer-order models do not account for. The motivation rests on the epidemiology of Nipah virus, a zoonotic pathogen the World Health Organization has classified as a priority pathogen requiring urgent research attention. Bats of the genus Pteropus serve as the primary natural reservoir, pigs act as intermediate hosts, and humans acquire infection through contaminated fruit, exposure to bat saliva or urine, contact with infected pigs, or human-to-human transmission in healthcare and family settings. No approved vaccine or targeted antiviral treatment exists, and patient management relies primarily on supportive care, with antiviral agents such as ribavirin showing limited effectiveness. The model divides human and pig populations into susceptible, infected, treated, and recovered compartments, while the bird population is partitioned into susceptible and infected classes. Transmission occurs through standard-incidence forces of infection that explicitly represent cross-species pathways: birds transmit to pigs and humans, pigs transmit to humans and within their own population, and infected humans contribute to further human spread. Birds act as the primary reservoir in the model’s biological assumptions, pigs serve as intermediate hosts capable of passing infection to humans, and treatment reduces disease burden without conferring immediate immunity. Discover more Learn Math Study Biology Check Symptoms Read Med Journals Track Outbreaks The Caputo fractional derivative of order between zero and one introduces a memory kernel that allows past states to influence current dynamics, capturing effects such as cumulative exposure, delayed disease progression, and behavioral adaptation. A uniform fractional order is assumed across all compartments for analytical consistency. The authors establish that solutions remain nonnegative and bounded within a biologically feasible region, prove existence and uniqueness of solutions via a fixed-point argument, and derive the disease-free equilibrium where all infected and treated compartments vanish. Using the next-generation matrix method, the team computed the basic reproduction number as the maximum of three host-specific thresholds, one each for humans, pigs, and birds. Because the underlying matrix is upper triangular, its eigenvalues fall on the diagonal, yielding a closed-form expression in which transmission coefficients and contact modification parameters appear in the numerator and treatment, natural mortality, and disease-induced mortality rates in the denominator. Sensitivity analysis shows that transmission rates and contact modification parameters carry positive sensitivity indices of one, making them the dominant drivers of disease spread, while treatment and removal rates reduce transmission. The stability analysis follows the fractional-order criterion that an equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable only when every eigenvalue of the linearized system satisfies an argument condition tied to the fractional order. The disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable when the reproduction number is below one and unstable when it exceeds one, with a Lyapunov-based argument extending this to global stability within the feasible region. When the reproduction number surpasses one, the authors show that a unique endemic equilibrium exists and can be locally stable under the same eigenvalue condition. Numerical simulations using a predictor-corrector Adams-Bashforth-Moulton scheme with a time step of 0.1 reveal a striking role for memory. Across scenarios testing fractional orders of 0.8, 0.9, and the classical integer-order case of 1, decreasing the fractional order significantly delayed epidemic peaks and prolonged infection duration, with the strongest sensitivity appearing in the human and pig populations. The abstract reports that reducing the fractional order lowered peak infection levels by more than 40 percent in some scenarios, while the classical case exhibited faster epidemic growth and quicker decay. The bird population showed monotone decline across all orders, though with markedly slower decline for smaller fractional values. Discover more infection Find Treatments Donate to Research Uninterruptible power supplies Applied science journals The optimal control framework introduces four time-dependent interventions bounded between zero and one: preventive measures reducing transmission to humans, intensified treatment for infected humans, biosecurity measures in pigs, and intensified treatment for infected pigs. Applying Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle yields a Hamiltonian, an adjoint system, and explicit characterizations of the optimal controls in terms of costate variables and infection forces. The objective functional balances the epidemiological burden of infection in each host population against quadratic costs of implementing each control. The simulation results carry a consistent practical message. Under optimal control, infected human and pig populations rapidly decline to near-zero levels in both disease-free and endemic settings, whereas uncontrolled dynamics show pronounced epidemic peaks followed by slow decay. Susceptible human and pig populations are better preserved under control, treated compartments attain substantially lower peaks, and phase portraits show controlled trajectories contracting toward the disease-free equilibrium while uncontrolled trajectories exhibit large persistent excursions. The optimal controls are strongest at early times and decrease thereafter, a front-loaded structure the authors interpret as evidence that early aggressive intervention is most effective. The authors frame the work as filling a gap in which existing models either focused on single-host dynamics without memory effects or applied fractional-order models to single populations without cross-species spillover mechanisms. They caution that the model is general rather than fitted to specific outbreak data: parameter values are taken from existing literature on Nipah virus dynamics or chosen to be biologically reasonable where empirical estimates are unavailable, no empirical datasets were generated or analyzed, and future work is expected to incorporate spatial heterogeneity, stochastic effects, and data-driven parameter estimation. Within those limits, the study argues that memory effects and coordinated, early interventions targeting both human and animal populations jointly shape whether a zoonotic spillover event fades out or persists. news.title_zh: 记忆效应和最优控制在分数多重 宿主 模型中重塑 尼帕病毒 跨物种溢出 - Bioengineer.org
news.source_body_en: A study published on 13 July 2026 in Discover Analytics by Sunday Oluwafemi Gbodogbe and Adedapo Chris Loyinmi developed a fractional-order epidemic model to analyze Nipah virus spillover across human, pig, and bird populations. The model incorporates memory effects from past infection states, which classical integer-order models do not account for. It uses the Caputo fractional derivative to represent these memory effects and includes cross-species transmission pathways. The study highlights that reducing the fractional order delayed epidemic peaks and prolonged infection duration, with peak infection levels lowered by over 40% in some scenarios. Birds showed a monotone decline across all fractional orders, though slower for smaller values. The authors emphasize the importance of early interventions to manage outbreaks, as optimal control strategies significantly reduced infected human and pig populations. However, the model is theoretical and not based on specific outbreak data, relying on existing literature for parameter values. The findings suggest that coordinated, early interventions targeting both human and animal populations can shape whether a zoonotic spillover event fades out or persists.

news.content: メインコンテンツへスキップ 40-100% Mortality Rate, No Vaccine. Decoding the Current State of 'Nipah Virus' in India Through Two Official Sources ohba.artlife Oct 28, 2026 17:45 Digest In the summer of 2025, four people were infected in Kerala, southern India (two of whom died). Then, in January 2026, two nurses were infected at a hospital in West Bengal, eastern India. Have you ever heard the name 'Nipah virus infection'? Its natural host is the bat, the mortality rate is 40-100%, and there are still no approved vaccines or treatments. Yet, it is also a 'distant disease' with not a single case reported in Japan so far. In this article, based on information from the WHO translated by the Quarantine Station of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (FORTH) and the latest commentary published in a medical journal, we will organize 'what is happening,' 'how it spreads,' and 'what travelers should be careful about' in a way that is understandable even with zero specialized knowledge. Table of Contents Digest Main Text What is Nipah virus infection in the first place? Summer 2025: 4 infected, 2 dead in Kerala Winter 2026: 2 nurses infected in West Bengal WHO risk assessment and what it means for us in Japan If you are traveling to India, pay attention to this Impressions Summary Sources すべて表示 Main Text What is Nipah virus infection in the first place? Nipah virus infection is a 'zoonotic disease' that spreads from animals to humans. The animals that carry the virus in nature are large bats called flying foxes (genus Pteropus). Humans become infected through intermediate animals like pigs, or by consuming fruits or date palm sap contaminated with bat saliva or urine. With the note that it is 'rare,' human-to-human transmission through close contact with infected individuals has also been reported. Progression of Symptoms It begins with symptoms that are difficult to distinguish from a cold or influenza, such as fever, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, and sore throat. Subsequently, neurological symptoms such as dizziness, drowsiness, and impaired consciousness appear, and if it becomes severe, it leads to acute encephalitis. According to commentary in a medical journal, severe cases can progress to coma within 24 to 48 hours of the onset of encephalitis or seizures. Incubation Period While there is a slight difference in the lower limit between the FORTH article, which states 'an average of about 4 to 14 days,' and the medical journal, which states '3 to 14 days,' both note that 'there are reports of up to 45 days.' In other words, the troublesome aspect of this disease is that it may manifest some time after returning home. Classification in Japan In Japan, it is designated as a 'Category IV Infectious Disease' under the Infectious Diseases Control Law, and doctors who diagnose it are obligated to report it to the public health center immediately. However, there has never been a report of Nipah virus infection within Japan to date. Summer 2025: 4 infected, 2 dead in Kerala The page published by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare Quarantine Station (FORTH) on October 20, 2025, is a translation of the 'Disease Outbreak News' issued by the WHO on August 6, 2025. The contents are summarized as follows. Period: May 17 to July 12, 2025 Location: Malappuram District (2 cases) and Palakkad District (2 cases) in Kerala Confirmed cases: 4 cases (2 of which were fatal) This is the first occurrence in Palakkad District. The four individuals had no epidemiological connection to each other and are considered 'spillover cases' where each was infected independently from the natural host (bats). It is reported that many flying foxes inhabit the affected areas. Kerala is a 'regular area' for Nipah Since the first outbreak in Kerala in 2018 (23 cases, 91% fatality rate), outbreaks have continued almost every year, including 2019, 2021, 2023, 2024, and 2025. As of July 2025, there have been 9 cumulative outbreaks in Kerala. While the WHO states that this is 'consistent with annual trends and not unexpected,' it assesses that localized risks remain in this region. Scale of local response As of July 17, 2025, a total of 723 contacts were identified. The breakdown is 394 in Palakkad District, 212 in Malappuram District, 114 in Kozhikode District, 2 in Ernakulam District, and 1 in Thrissur District. 26 special teams were deployed for contact tracing and health monitoring, and special alerts were issued to hospitals in multiple districts. Winter 2026: 2 nurses infected in West Bengal A series in the medical journal 'Web Medical Journal' (published February 26, 2026) covers a new report that occurred subsequently. The author is an infectious disease specialist belonging to a national infectious disease research institution. January 26, 2026, India's IHR (International Health Regulations) National Focal Point reported to the WHO Location: The same private hospital in Barasat, West Bengal Infected individuals: Two nurses in their 20s and 30s Onset of symptoms in late December 2025, hospitalized in early January 2026 Confirmed on January 13 at the National Institute of Virology in Pune via RT-PCR and antibody testing (ELISA) One patient is in critical condition requiring a ventilator, while the other recovered after exhibiting severe neurological symptoms Testing of over 190 contacts resulted in all being negative. This is the third outbreak in West Bengal, following those in 2001 (Siliguri) and 2007 (Nadia). Points of concern These two individuals are healthcare workers, and the route of infection is currently unknown. While the four cases in Kerala are believed to have been 'each infected from nature,' the fact that 'it is unknown where they were infected' is why this is drawing the attention of experts. There are reports that some countries, such as Thailand and Taiwan, are strengthening their alert status. WHO risk assessment and what it means for us in Japan The WHO assesses the risk of this 2026 outbreak as 'moderate at the local level, and low at the national, regional, and global levels.' Regarding the 2025 Kerala outbreak, it also stated that the risk of international spread is low and does not recommend restrictions on travel or trade with India. On the other hand, due to its high mortality rate, the Nipah virus is included in the WHO's 'list of priority pathogens that could cause future outbreaks or pandemics.' In today's world of easy travel, the possibility of imported cases being reported in Japan is not zero—this is the assessment of commentators in medical journals. If you are traveling to India, pay attention to this Based on FORTH's 'To those traveling abroad,' here is a summary of practical precautions. Before traveling Check local outbreak status and medical information through official sources such as FORTH and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consult a travel clinic if necessary. During travel Basic infection control measures such as hand washing, alcohol disinfection, masks, and cough etiquette are also effective against the Nipah virus Avoid visiting pig farms or having direct contact with pigs Do not consume unwashed raw fruits, fruits with bite marks from bats, or raw date palm sap or juice Do not approach areas known as bat roosts Avoid contact with people who have been confirmed or are suspected of being infected If you develop suspicious symptoms such as fever, headache, dizziness, or neurological symptoms, seek medical attention at a local facility immediately and be sure to report your travel history and activities in the area After returning to Japan If you feel unwell upon returning, report your travel history and activities to the quarantine station at the airport or port and consult with them. Monitor your health for about 14 days after returning, and if you notice any abnormalities, go to a medical institution. Be sure to inform them of your travel history when you visit. Impressions What struck me while comparing these two official and professional sources was that even with the "same virus in the same country," the "quality" of the situation in Kerala and West Bengal is completely different. Because outbreaks occur almost every year in Kerala, the protocols and contact tracing systems are well-established, demonstrating a capacity to track 723 people. On the other hand, in the West Bengal case, healthcare workers were infected, and the route of transmission is unknown. Although the number is only two, it is natural for experts to focus on this. That said, the WHO's assessment is consistently that the "international risk is low." There is no need to be overly fearful; if you are traveling to India, you can avoid most risks simply by following the basic rule of "staying away from bats, pigs, and raw sap." Perhaps the right way to maintain perspective on this disease is to focus on the "narrowness" of the transmission routes rather than being captivated by the high mortality rate. 🙂🙂 If you have read this far, you must be a person of inquiry. If you would like, please support me with a 'Like' ♥️👍🏻 or a 'Follow' ♥️👍🏻; it would be very encouraging! 🙂🙂 ※ Images and similar content are used from the sources. Summary Nipah virus infection is a zoonotic disease for which fruit bats are the natural host. The mortality rate is 40-100%, and there are no approved vaccines or treatments yet. Between May and July 2025, there were 4 cases (2 deaths) in Kerala, India. These were independent infections unrelated to each other, and 723 contacts were traced. In January 2026, two nurses were infected at a private hospital in West Bengal. One is in serious condition on a ventilator, and one has recovered. All 190+ contacts tested negative, but the route of infection is unknown. The WHO risk assessment is "moderate at the local level, and low at the national, regional, and global levels." Travel and trade restrictions to India are not recommended. In Japan, it is a Category IV infectious disease. There have been zero domestic reports to date, but the possibility of imported cases has been pointed out. Countermeasures when traveling include "avoiding raw fruit, date palm sap, pigs, and bat roosts," "basic infection control measures," and "14-day health observation and reporting travel history after returning home." Sources Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare Quarantine Station FORTH "Nipah Virus Infection - India (August 6, 2025)" (Published October 20, 2025) https://www.forth.go.jp/topics/2025/20251020_00001.html Japan Medical Journal Web Medical Journal "Nipah Virus Infection Reported in 2 Healthcare Workers from India [Infectious Disease Past and Present - Trending Infectious Disease Pickup - (44)]" Masahiro Ishigane (Published February 26, 2026) https://www.jmedj.co.jp/blogs/product/product_28167 Disclaimer This article is organized based on publicly available information and is not intended for medical diagnosis or advice. We do not guarantee the accuracy or completeness of the content, and the use of this information is at your own discretion and risk. Please consult a medical institution if you have any concerns about your health. #インド #感染 #ニパウイルス #インド #感染 #ニパウイルス トップ 健康・医療 病気 ピックアップされています 気になる記事のマッシュアップ 1,775件 ニュース、本、情報、等の雑感 372件

During travel Basic infection control measures such as hand washing, alcohol disinfection, masks, and cough etiquette are also effective against the Nipah virus Avoid visiting pig farms or having direct contact with pigs Do not consume unwashed raw fruits, fruits with bite marks from bats, or raw date palm sap or juice Do not approach areas known as bat roosts Avoid contact with people who have been confirmed or are suspected of being infected If you develop suspicious symptoms such as fever, headache, dizziness, or neurological symptoms, seek medical attention at a local facility immediately and be sure to report your travel history and activities in the area After returning to Japan If you feel unwell upon returning, report your travel history and activities to the quarantine station at the airport or port and consult with them. Monitor your health for about 14 days after returning, and if you notice any abnormalities, go to a medical institution. Be sure to inform them of your travel history when you visit. Impressions What struck me while comparing these two official and professional sources was that even with the "same virus in the same country," the "quality" of the situation in Kerala and West Bengal is completely different. Because outbreaks occur almost every year in Kerala, the protocols and contact tracing systems are well-established, demonstrating a capacity to track 723 people. On the other hand, in the West Bengal case, healthcare workers were infected, and the route of transmission is unknown. Although the number is only two, it is natural for experts to focus on this. That said, the WHO's assessment is consistently that the "international risk is low." There is no need to be overly fearful; if you are traveling to India, you can avoid most risks simply by following the basic rule of "staying away from bats, pigs, and raw sap." Perhaps the right way to maintain perspective on this disease is to focus on the "narrowness" of the transmission routes rather than being captivated by the high mortality rate. 🙂🙂 If you have read this far, you must be a person of inquiry. If you would like, please support me with a 'Like' ♥️👍🏻 or a 'Follow' ♥️👍🏻; it would be very encouraging! 🙂🙂 ※ Images and similar content are used from the sources. Summary Nipah virus infection is a zoonotic disease for which fruit bats are the natural host. The mortality rate is 40-100%, and there are no approved vaccines or treatments yet. Between May and July 2025, there were 4 cases (2 deaths) in Kerala, India. These were independent infections unrelated to each other, and 723 contacts were traced. In January 2026, two nurses were infected at a private hospital in West Bengal. One is in serious condition on a ventilator, and one has recovered. All 190+ contacts tested negative, but the route of infection is unknown. The WHO risk assessment is "moderate at the local level, and low at the national, regional, and global levels." Travel and trade restrictions to India are not recommended. In Japan, it is a Category IV infectious disease. There have been zero domestic reports to date, but the possibility of imported cases has been pointed out. Countermeasures when traveling include "avoiding raw fruit, date palm sap, pigs, and bat roosts," "basic infection control measures," and "14-day health observation and reporting travel history after returning home." Aswin J Kumar Published: November 02, 2026 02:23 PM IST 4 minute Read In Brief In Brief Summary is AI-generated × The probe announced into whether expired Remdesivir was given to Nipah patients faces potential delays due to a conflict of interest, as the appointed panel head previously served as the convenor of the Nipah Medical Board. The Health Minister's admission that expired doses may have been administered between 2023 and 2025 has sparked a political controversy, challenging the government's claims of exemplary outbreak management. Former health experts and treating doctors have disputed the allegations, highlighting that multiple cross-verification checks exist and that Remdesivir batches had varying expiry dates extending beyond 2023. Share × Copy Link Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Reddit Comments 0% Follow Us The probe announced by Keralam Health Minister K Muraleedharan to find out if expired doses of Remdesivir were given to Nipah patients may be delayed due to a possible conflict of interest. While announcing an expert panel headed by Dr Aravind Reghukumar, Head of the Department of Infectious Diseases, Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram, the government seems to have overlooked the fact that Dr Aravind had been the convenor of the Medical Board for Nipah disease. Whenever an outbreak is confirmed, the Medical Board convenes regularly and finalises a host of aspects including contact tracing, drug availability, quarantine and other probable situations arising out of disease spread. All these meetings were held with Dr Aravind in attendance. Sources said that Dr Aravind has not been given any formal orders to begin the probe. Besides, he is learnt to have communicated about the situation to the Directorate of Medical Education. Dr Aravind said he cannot comment on the matter. Meanwhile, officials with the Office of the Health Minister said that in the wake of allegations about expired drugs being given to patients, a probe has become imperative. The minister's reply kicked up a political row in the state as the LDF government had often touted Nipah management as exemplary, which brought down the case fatality rate (CFR) from 91% to 33% in the recent outbreaks reported in 2023 and 2025. In his reply to a submission in the Kerala Assembly, the minister, quoting figures from Kozhikode Medical College, made serious statements about administering Remdesivir. According to his reply, KMSCL (Kerala Medical Services Corporation Limited) had last bought Remdesivir in June 2021, and these medicines had an expiry date of May 30, 2023. These medicines were used in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (102 vials in 2023, 34 vials in 2024 and 10 in 2025). The minister said that the committee will look into whether Nipah patients died because of using expired medicine and whether other patients complained of any side effects. Former health experts associated with Nipah management in Keralam as well as doctors who had taken Remdesivir as a prophylactic while treating Nipah patients said that the minister's statement is problematic in many ways. ADVERTISEMENT Remdesivir was procured from multiple agencies by the state government in 2021 to manage the second wave of COVID-19. "These batches had different expiry dates -- 2023 and 2025. The allegation stems from the assumption that one batch expired in 2023 and hence the expiry period is two years, which is not the case. Also, the KMSCL has a default system which flags expired medicines before it is supplied. It's not just patients, but several doctors had also used this medicine as a preventive, and it is highly improbable that none of them would check the expiry date," Dr Anish T S, former Nodal Officer for the Kerala One Health Centre for Nipah Research and Resilience, told Onmanorama. It's a broad-spectrum antiviral which has been considered a safe drug. Between 2023 and 2026, 6 Nipah patients were given this medicine and all of them survived. There are multiple levels to check the expiry of this drug, he added. A doctor who treated a Nipah patient told Onmanorama that he had been administered Remdesivir and he was certain that the drug was within the expiry date. Onmanorama tried to contact two former officials responsible for procurement and supply of this drug during COVID period, but they didn't respond. The Nipah management plan for Kozhikode prepared by the Health Department in 2021 notes that no approved drugs or vaccines were currently available and that there was an unmet need for newer therapeutic options for NiV(Nipah virus) infection. "In diseases like NiV infection, any new drug can be tried only during an outbreak situation and that too strictly adhering to the clinical trial protocol," it said. The treatment algorithm also showed “considering” use of MAB (Monoclonal Antibody) Remdesivir/Favipiravir/Ribavirin after discussion with the patient, and that the treatment plan has to be formulated by the Institutional Medical Board. The resource group, which prepared this document, also included Dr Aravind. The treatment protocol published in 2023 also lists Remdesivir for broad-spectrum antiviral activity. While the minister's statement was mainly based on information from Kozhikode Medical College, officials said that the medicines were supplied to three other hospitals where the disease was confirmed. According to former officials who managed Nipah, the drug details, including the expiry date, are entered on software by the store superintendent and the pharmacist, and the drug reaches the patient only after cross-verification by the nursing officers. Another report has also emerged which says that an American company had supplied Remdesivir without a manufacturing date. Officials said that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) insists on an expiration date on a drug product, but does not explicitly mandate a manufacturing (MFG) date on the label. The government has not responded to this allegation. Aswin J Kumar Published: November 02, 2026 02:23 PM IST 4 minute Read In Brief In Brief Summary is AI-generated × The probe announced into whether expired Remdesivir was given to Nipah patients faces potential delays due to a conflict of interest, as the appointed panel head previously served as the convenor of the Nipah Medical Board. The Health Minister's admission that expired doses may have been administered between 2023 and 2025 has sparked a political controversy, challenging the government's claims of exemplary outbreak management. Former health experts and treating doctors have disputed the allegations, highlighting that multiple cross-verification checks exist and that Remdesivir batches had varying expiry dates extending beyond 2023. Share × Copy Link Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Reddit Comments 0% Follow Us The probe announced by Keralam Health Minister K Muraleedharan to find out if expired doses of Remdesivir were given to Nipah patients may be delayed due to a possible conflict of interest. While announcing an expert panel headed by Dr Aravind Reghukumar, Head of the Department of Infectious Diseases, Government Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram, the government seems to have overlooked the fact that Dr Aravind had been the convenor of the Medical Board for Nipah disease. Whenever an outbreak is confirmed, the Medical Board convenes regularly and finalises a host of aspects including contact tracing, drug availability, quarantine and other probable situations arising out of disease spread. All these meetings were held with Dr Aravind in attendance. Sources said that Dr Aravind has not been given any formal orders to begin the probe. Besides, he is learnt to have communicated about the situation to the Directorate of Medical Education. Dr Aravind said he cannot comment on the matter. Meanwhile, officials with the Office of the Health Minister said that in the wake of allegations about expired drugs being given to patients, a probe has become imperative. The minister's reply kicked up a political row in the state as the LDF government had often touted Nipah management as exemplary, which brought down the case fatality rate (CFR) from 91% to 33% in the recent outbreaks reported in 2023 and 2025. In his reply to a submission in the Kerala Assembly, the minister, quoting figures from Kozhikode Medical College, made serious statements about administering Remdesivir. According to his reply, KMSCL (Kerala Medical Services Corporation Limited) had last bought Remdesivir in June 2021, and these medicines had an expiry date of May 30, 2023. These medicines were used in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (102 vials in 2023, 34 vials in 2024 and 10 in 2025). The minister said that the committee will look into whether Nipah patients died because of using expired medicine and whether other patients complained of any side effects. Former health experts associated with Nipah management in Keralam as well as doctors who had taken Remdesivir as a prophylactic while treating Nipah patients said that the minister's statement is problematic in many ways. ADVERTISEMENT Remdesivir was procured from multiple agencies by the state government in 2021 to manage the second wave of COVID-19. "These batches had different expiry dates -- 2023 and 2025. The allegation stems from the assumption that one batch expired in 2023 and hence the expiry period is two years, which is not the case. Also, the KMSCL has a default system which flags expired medicines before it is supplied. It's not just patients, but several doctors had also used this medicine as a preventive, and it is highly improbable that none of them would check the expiry date," Dr Anish T S, former Nodal Officer for the Kerala One Health Centre for Nipah Research and Resilience, told Onmanorama. It's a broad-spectrum antiviral which has been considered a safe drug. Between 2023 and 2026, 6 Nipah patients were given this medicine and all of them survived. There are multiple levels to check the expiry of this drug, he added. A doctor who treated a Nipah patient told Onmanorama that he had been administered Remdesivir and he was certain that the drug was within the expiry date. Onmanorama tried to contact two former officials responsible for procurement and supply of this drug during COVID period, but they didn't respond. The Nipah management plan for Kozhikode prepared by the Health Department in 2021 notes that no approved drugs or vaccines were currently available and that there was an unmet need for newer therapeutic options for NiV(Nipah virus) infection. "In diseases like NiV infection, any new drug can be tried only during an outbreak situation and that too strictly adhering to the clinical trial protocol," it said. The treatment algorithm also showed “considering” use of MAB (Monoclonal Antibody) Remdesivir/Favipiravir/Ribavirin after discussion with the patient, and that the treatment plan has to be formulated by the Institutional Medical Board. The resource group, which prepared this document, also included Dr Aravind. The treatment protocol published in 2023 also lists Remdesivir for broad-spectrum antiviral activity. While the minister's statement was mainly based on information from Kozhikode Medical College, officials said that the medicines were supplied to three other hospitals where the disease was confirmed. According to former officials who managed Nipah, the drug details, including the expiry date, are entered on software by the store superintendent and the pharmacist, and the drug reaches the patient only after cross-verification by the nursing officers. Another report has also emerged which says that an American company had supplied Remdesivir without a manufacturing date. Officials said that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) insists on an expiration date on a drug product, but does not explicitly mandate a manufacturing (MFG) date on the label. The government has not responded to this allegation. news.content: ANIMAL RESEARCH NEWS - OCTOBER 2026 The Biomedical Animal Research News (BARN) Digest collates animal research news from Concordat on Openness signatories and UAR’s 150+ member organisations into one, easy to access, feed. These animal research related stories include topics such as: basic biological research; medical studies and advancements; animal welfare and 3Rs news; funding, regulatory, and policy news; and conservation and environmental research that involves animal testing. Each month, we pick the most interesting, groundbreaking, and important news to feature in a monthly news roundup. View BARN to see daily news updates from UAR members. BASIC/DISCOVERY RESEARCH New gene-editing approach shows promise in treating Huntington's disease in mice CARDIFF UNIVERSITY | MICE "A team of researchers led by Cardiff University has developed a promising new gene-editing approach that could transform the treatment of Huntington’s disease in the future. In the new study, published in Science Translational Medicine , researchers used a more precise gene-editing enzyme called Cas9 nickase, which cuts only a single strand of DNA within the repeated CAG/CTG sequences in mouse models of Huntington’s disease. Professor Dion said: “When packaged into viral vectors and delivered directly to the striatum - the brain region primarily impacted by Huntington's disease - in a mouse model, the therapy shortened the DNA repeats in the majority of targeted neurons. “This led to fewer toxic Huntington protein aggregates, restored healthier gene expression pathways in brain cells, and showed significant improvements in motor function during locomotion tests.” The team say no unwanted mutations were detected in brain cells in the mouse models with this approach, and it offers a potentially safer alternative to conventional gene-editing methods." https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/news/view/3114425-new-gene-editing-approach-shows-promise-in-treating-huntingtons-disease-in-mice Smoking alters reproductive organs in both men and women, new study finds UNIVERSITY OF SHEFFIELD | MICE "A new study, led by researchers from the Universities of Sheffield and Nottingham examined how different levels of cigarette smoke exposure affect the reproductive organs of male and female mice. Male and female mice were exposed to cigarette smoke extract at a lower or higher dose for 12 weeks. Researchers then examined the structure of the ovaries and testes and measured gene activity in each. The findings offer valuable insight into the biological processes that may help explain how smoking affects reproductive health in humans. In females, the number and structure of ovarian follicles, where eggs develop, showed relatively little change following exposure, even at higher levels. However, smoke exposure reduced the activity of genes responsible for cell division and metabolism, while increasing the activity of genes that control protein production. These shifts mirror biological changes typically seen in accelerated ovarian ageing and declining fertility in women. In males, higher levels of smoke exposure led to physical changes inside the testes, including the enlargement of the seminiferous tubules where sperm develop. Genes regulating sperm production become over active, while genes that protect against infection and inflammation became less active. These results suggest that cigarette smoke directly disrupts essential biological processes essential for healthy testicular function and sperm development." https://sheffield.ac.uk/news/smoking-alters-reproductive-organs-both-men-and-women-new-study-finds Scientists are a step closer to understanding and extending lifespan QUEEN MARY UNIVERSITY OF LONDON | WORMS, FLIES "Scientists have taken an important step towards understanding how the biological processes of ageing might one day be targeted to help people live healthier for longer. Research involving Queen Mary University of London has found that directly activating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) – an ancient enzyme that helps cells respond when energy levels are low – extended lifespan in three very different organisms: fruit flies, nematode worms and fission yeast. The study, published in Aging Cell , provides new evidence that AMPK could be a potential target for future research into longevity and healthy ageing." https://www.qmul.ac.uk/news/latest-news/2026/science-and-engineering/se/scientists-are-a-step-closer-to-understanding-and-extending-lifespan.html Clearing ‘immune fog’ could stop lung cancer years before diagnosis UCL | HUMAN SAMPLES, MICE "A ‘rising fog’ that may cloud the immune system’s ability to detect tumours, potentially helping lung cancer develop years before diagnosis has been discovered by UCL researchers. Published in the journal Nature , the research adds to growing evidence that one day cancer could be targeted before it even develops, rather than waiting until the disease causes noticeable symptoms, and in cases of advanced cancer, be harder to treat. The team carefully studied blood and tissue samples collected from people taking part in long-running lung cancer surveillance and screening studies, while also analysing similar processes in mice, to understand what makes precursors of lung cancer (called pre-cancers or lesions) develop into fully-fledged tumours. They discovered regulatory T cells (Tregs), a set of specialised cells that form part of the immune system, were gradually building up months or years before cancer develops. Tregs typically hold back other cells in the immune system, pausing their activity, which could be allowing pre-cancers to slip through the cracks and develop into lung cancer unchallenged by the immune system. Using prototype blood tests, the team found that monitoring the levels of Tregs in the blood could help to identify people at increasing risk of lung cancer or patients with a very early form of the disease. It also explored using targeted cancer drugs to reverse and disperse the Treg “fog” and found that a drug targeting specific immune processes could reverse the Treg’s immune-suppressing effect, halving the proportion of animals that developed lung tumours in laboratory experiments, and preventing formation of all large tumours." https://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/2026/oct/clearing-immune-fog-could-stop-lung-cancer-years-diagnosis Study unlocks key immune cells in pigs to advance vaccine research THE PIRBRIGHT INSTITUTE | PIGS "Researchers from The Pirbright Institute have developed new tools to identify and study a critical group of immune cells in pigs that help generate protective antibodies following vaccination and infection. The breakthrough is an important step in using pigs as a model for vaccine development and could help accelerate the design and evaluation of vaccines for both animal and human health. Published in the Journal of Immunology , the study focuses on T follicular helper (Tfh) cells - specialised immune cells that play a central role in helping B cells produce high-quality antibodies. “Our study revealed that pig Tfh and Tfr cells share many of the same characteristics seen in humans and mice, highlighting important similarities between species and reinforcing the value of pigs as a model for understanding vaccine-induced immunity.”" https://www.pirbright.ac.uk/news/study-unlocks-key-immune-cells-pigs-advance-vaccine-research ANIMAL BEHAVIOUR AND WELFARE New BBSRC funding to build a foundation AI model that can learn the 'language' of mouse behaviour SAINSBURYS WELLCOME CENTRE, BBSRC | MICE "Dr Dario Campagner and Professor Tiago Branco at the Sainsbury Wellcome Centre (SWC) have been granted new BBSRC funding. The award will support the team to create an open-source AI model that recognises and describes patterns in animal behaviour with unprecedented detail. The aim is to better characterise behavioural traits, detect changes over time, compare results across studies, species and mouse models for diseases, and link behaviour to brain activity. The model is expected to benefit neuroscience, preclinical and ecological research. “Foundation models are extremely powerful because they can learn complex structure from very large and complex datasets, but their success depends on having enough high-quality training data,” said Dr Dario Campagner, Aeon Group Leader and Senior Research Fellow at SWC. “Thanks to the Aeon platform, we have now collected hundreds of billions of frames of mouse behaviour across a wide range of natural and learned behaviours, all recorded in a consistent format. This puts us in a unique position to train a general model of mouse behaviour and, importantly, to make it openly available so that researchers can adapt it to their own experiments and scientific questions.” https://www.sainsburywellcome.org/research-news/new-bbsrc-funding-build-foundation-ai-model-can-learn-language-mouse-behaviour Discovery of chicken immune cells could pave the way for more effective poultry vaccines UNIVERSITY OF BRISTOL | CHICKENS "A previously unknown population of immune cells in chickens has been discovered by researchers from the University of Bristol Veterinary School in collaboration with The Pirbright Institute. The finding could help transform the way poultry vaccines are developed. The study, published in the European Journal of Immunology , is the first to identify and characterise lipid-reactive Natural Killer T (NKT)-like cells in birds." https://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2026/october/discovery-of-chicken-immune-cells-and-effective-poultry-vaccines.html Dual-protection vaccine to reduce risk of Nipah virus outbreaks THE PIRBRIGHT INSTITUTE | PIGS "The Pirbright Institute is leading an international three-year project funded by the UK Vaccine Network to develop a pioneering bivalent vaccine that protects pigs against Nipah virus and pseudorabies. Addressing a critical gap in global animal and public health preparedness, the project - Duo-ProTectz - builds on earlier research that showed a vaccine candidate could protect pigs against both diseases. Nipah virus is a highly pathogenic zoonotic virus that can spread from animals to humans and has been identified by the World Health Organization as a priority pathogen with epidemic and pandemic potential. The most severe recorded outbreak, in Malaysia in 1998 to 99, was linked to pig-to-human transmission and resulted in the culling of more than one million pigs, causing economic losses estimated at £433 million ($582m USD). Led by Professor Simon Graham , Head of Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (PRRS) Immunology at The Pirbright Institute, the work will focus on demonstrating the vaccine's commercial viability through further manufacturing, safety and efficacy studies, alongside the development of a companion diagnostic test." https://www.pirbright.ac.uk/news/dual-protection-vaccine-reduce-risk-nipah-virus-outbreaks REPLACING ANIMALS IN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH Pioneering human-relevant approaches across immunotherapy, oncology and gene therapy - NC3RS PRIZE NC3RS | NON-ANIMAL METHODS "This year’s International 3Rs Prize recognises advances in complex in vitro models that enable the replacement of animals and generate new insights into human disease. The Prize recognises a primary research paper, published between September 2022 and September 2025, that contributes to the 3Rs. It is sponsored by GSK as part of its long-standing support of the Prize. With submissions spanning all three ‘Rs’ and representing researchers from the UK, Ireland, Europe and the USA, the breadth and quality of applications made the final decision especially challenging. Alongside the winner, the Panel have also recognised two highly commended publications. Read about the pioneering human-relevant replacement approaches recognised by this year’s International 3Rs Prize below. Over the coming weeks we will be sharing interviews with our winning and highly commended researchers, discussing the science behind their work, the challenges they have overcome and the impact they are making on replacing the use of animals. https://nc3rs.org.uk/news/pioneering-human-relevant-approaches-across-immunotherapy-oncology-and-gene-therapy Visit BARN for daily news updates Last edited: 29 October 2026 09:50 Back to News

analysis.location_and_population: United Kingdom, involving mice and human participants in lung cancer studies.
analysis.event: A monthly animal research news digest was published by Understanding Animal Research, featuring studies on gene-editing for Huntington's disease, effects of smoking on reproductive organs, and immune processes in lung cancer development.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The studies involved mice models and human participants in lung cancer surveillance. No confirmed cases, deaths, or exposures related to the Nipah virus were reported. The research focused on biological processes and potential therapeutic applications.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The news digest is a summary of ongoing research and does not indicate any outbreak or public health response. The studies are in the preliminary or exploratory stage, with no confirmed or suspected cases of Nipah virus reported.

analysis.brief_en: In October 2026, Understanding Animal Research published a monthly digest of animal research news, highlighting studies on gene-editing for Huntington's disease, the impact of smoking on reproductive organs, and immune processes in lung cancer development. The digest includes research from Cardiff University, the University of Sheffield, Queen Mary University of London, and The Pirbright Institute, all involving mice models. These studies focus on biological mechanisms and potential therapeutic applications, with no confirmed or suspected cases of Nipah virus reported. The findings are in the preliminary stage, and the research does not indicate any outbreak or public health response. The studies aim to advance medical understanding and treatment options for various conditions, with no evidence of Nipah virus-related events in the provided content.

news.content: ☰ Home page » News » Kerala » Nipah Medicine Row Nipah antiviral row: Kerala Health Minister promises action following expert panel probe Published By: News Desk Last Updated: 30 October 2026, 01:08 PM IST Follow us on Kerala Health Minister K. Muraleedharan | Photo: Mathrubhumi Thiruvananthapuram: Health Minister K Muraleedharan on Friday stated that the Kerala government would take further action upon receiving a report from an expert committee investigating allegations that expired doses of Remdesivir were administered to Nipah patients in the state in previous years. The probe follows a submission by Congress MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan in the State Assembly on Thursday. Replying to the submission, the minister noted that Remdesivir procured in 2021 carried an expiry date of May 2023, yet reports suggest it might have been administered to patients admitted to Kozhikode Medical College until 2025. Speaking to reporters, Muraleedharan clarified that the information presented to the Assembly was sourced from official reports provided by Health Department authorities, emphasizing that he would refrain from making further comments until the expert panel submits its findings. He assured that the government would investigate whether the deaths of Nipah patients were linked to the administration of expired medication, and whether other patients who received the drug suffered any adverse side effects. "There are several doubts regarding the medicine, including whether it was administered after its expiry date. We will investigate and take a decision," he said. The minister clarified that the investigation focuses strictly on whether expired doses were administered to patients, rather than any concerns regarding the inherent quality or efficacy of Remdesivir. Recalling the procurement of the antiviral during a prior Nipah outbreak after the UDF government assumed power, he noted that initial attempts to source the drug from various parts of the country failed because available stocks in Mumbai had already expired. Subsequently, the Kerala Medical Services Corporation Limited (KMSCL) informed the government that valid stock was available in Bahrain, after which it was airlifted within 48 hours. He highlighted that patients who received the medicine within its validity period recovered, reiterating that the issue centers on expiry management rather than the drug's therapeutic capability. Muraleedharan stated that an expert panel headed by Dr Aravind would conduct an impartial investigation without preconceived conclusions. The panel's mandate includes auditing how the drug was procured and distributed, examining the role of intermediaries, and reviewing the operational functioning of KMSCL. The government will also look into whether any private agents were involved in the procurement chain. Additionally, the Kozhikode Medical College superintendent informed the minister that while the Remdesivir packaging listed an expiry date, it omitted the manufacturing date—a standard requirement on pharmaceutical packaging. This discrepancy will also be investigated. The government is further reviewing reports that the medicine supplied to patients was labeled for clinical trial use, though an authoritative report on this aspect is awaited. "Further decisions on the issues would be taken after receiving the expert committee's findings," Muraleedharan said. He added that concerns regarding the involvement of foreign pharmaceutical firms in the state's procurement procedures would be thoroughly examined. Procurement records and mortality timeline Detailed procurement records reveal that KMSCL last acquired 3,000 vials of Remdesivir via its Karunya scheme on June 3, 2021, at a cost of ₹42 lakh, carrying an official expiry date of May 30, 2023. Data provided by Kozhikode Medical College Hospital indicates that 102 vials were utilised during 2023–24, 34 vials during 2024–25, 10 vials during 2025–26, and 50 vials during 2026–27. However, the 50 vials used during 2026–27 were freshly procured from Bahrain on June 12, 2026, specifically to treat a Nipah patient. These timelines have raised strong suspicions that the Remdesivir administered at the medical college throughout 2023, 2024, and 2025 had already passed its expiration date. Consequently, instructions have been issued to the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) and the Directorate of Health Services (DHS) to compile comprehensive records of all patients who received Remdesivir across state health facilities during these periods. The state recorded six Nipah cases in 2023, resulting in two fatalities. In 2024, two cases were reported, both of which were fatal. In 2025, two out of three reported Nipah patients succumbed to the infection. In 2026, one Nipah case was reported, and the patient successfully recovered. Nipah virus is a zoonotic pathogen capable of transmission between animals and humans. Fruit bats (flying foxes) serve as the primary natural reservoir for the virus, which can also infect swine and human populations.
